title: Fix the self-referential SY-3 timeout-message assertion in sync_orchestrator_test.dart — it never calls SyncOrchestratorImpl

evidence.quote:
const message = 'Sync timed out — tap to retry';
      expect(message, contains('timed out'));

why: The test declares its own local `message` string literal and asserts it contains 'timed out' — guaranteed true by the literal it just wrote — then compares a bare TimeoutException.toString() against that same local constant. It never touches SyncOrchestratorImpl or its catch block, so it provides zero protection for the orchestrator's actual TimeoutException-handling path. A maintainer reading this file alone would believe SY-3's friendly-timeout-message behavior is covered right here. Genuine end-to-end coverage of the same behavior does exist, but in a different file (test/sync/sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart, outside this batch) — this copy is dead weight that would mask a real gap if that sibling file were ever trimmed or moved.
recommendation: Delete this test (real coverage lives in test/sync/sy3_sync_error_message_sanitize_test.dart) or rewrite it to call orchestrator.pullOnLaunch() with a TimeoutException-throwing fake gateway and assert on the emitted SyncStatusError.message, matching the pattern used two tests above it in this same file.
acceptance_criteria: Test either removed with the reason in the commit message (TQ-7) or rewritten to drive pullOnLaunch() through a timeout-throwing fake gateway and assert the resulting SyncStatusError.message
